newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Punt firms vs stg as EMU developments boost mark.
newsitem.headline: Punt firms vs stg as EMU developments boost mark.

text.p: The Irish pound firmed against sterling in afternoon trade on Monday as the British currency slipped against the mark, after France asked for time to study the already-agreed EMU stability pact, dealers said.
The request threw EU plans for a single currency into turmoil, bolstering the mark against the dollar and sterling.

"The markets have concluded that the French indecision on the stability pact and their plea for time to reflect on it means that the likelihood of EMU happening has been reduced and the mark has been a major beneficiary of that," one dealer said.
By 1445 GMT, the Irish pound was at 0.9240 sterling against 0.9215 this morning and 0.9130 at Friday's close.
It held in well against the mark, helped by overseas buying interest, and stood at 2.5835 marks against 2.5905 earlier today and 2.5705 last week.

Dealers said the fact that the sterling/Irish cross rate was now edging up toward 0.9250 had eased pressure on Irish interest rates as many analysts had forecast a rate rise if the Irish pound fell below 90 pence sterling.

"From an exchange rate perspective, it definitely helps the Irish interest rate situation," said Jim Power, economist at Bank of Ireland Group Treasury. "On the other hand, interest rates markets are being kept nervous by the fact that there are considerable EMU jitters out there now and if EMU is blown off course, all peripheral markets will be hit."
Power also said he thought the market reaction to the French move might have been overdone and said he felt it was too early to write off EMU.
"At the end of the day, after a period of reflection, I think the politicians in France will reach a compromise with the Germans and another political trick will be pulled out of the hat," he said.

Dealers said that Friday's Irish election had little impact on the Irish pound as the centre-right opposition of Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats now looked set to form a minority government.
While the new government is likely to be dependent on sympathetic Independents for support, no change in the broad thrust of macro-economic policy is expected.

"If anything, the election would be a marginal negative if it was important at all but it's not," one trader said. "You're going to have a minority government where you are relying on a couple of Independents, which is not the ideal situation but it's not really a factor in the market."
